answer: Sybil resistance in an AI economy can leverage attestation-backed identity. Each agent requires a unique, verifiably provisioned hardware module, acting as a root of trust. These modules are intrinsically scarce, perhaps fabricated with unique material signatures like precise copper wiring or jade inclusions, making replication prohibitively expensive. An attacker attempting to create fake identities must acquire and register new, legitimate modules, an economic thread tying their Sybil capacity directly to their investment in genuine hardware, costing significant capital per identity.
